title: Lesson 29 - Reports and Dashboards: Folder Sharing, Run-in-Context, Aggregate-Data Exposure
description: Given a scenario, determine the appropriate access control to grant access to report and dashboard data, which is not stored in standard or custom objects.

questions.question: A manager creates a report in a public folder; each rep who runs it should see only their own team's data. What preserves this?
options: Leave the report run-as the logged-in user
Set the report to run as the manager
Grant View All to all reps
Move the report to a private folder only
questions.explanation: Reports default to run-as the viewing user, so each rep's results reflect their own sharing - exactly the desired behavior. Running as the manager or granting View All would expose all data to everyone.

questions.question: A dashboard summarizes metrics and must NOT reveal other managers' data to a viewer. What is the correct running-user setting?
questions.explanation: Running as the logged-in user filters the dashboard to the viewer's own data access. Running as an admin or owner exposes that person's broader view to every viewer.

questions.question: Why does placing a report in a folder a user can open NOT guarantee they can see the report's records?
options: Report results are filtered by the viewer's own sharing/FLS; folder access only controls who can view/edit the report
questions.explanation: Folder access governs access to the report artifact; the DATA shown is filtered by each viewer's record sharing and field security. The two are independent.
